what: Sanyasi rebellion of the 1770s-90s: bands of sanyasis defeated sepoys; Elliot (1789) calls them usurers disguised as religious friars; Warren Hastings 1773 letter on a band that cut off two officers.
quote: These people are described in a long minute of John Elliot, dated 29th April 1789, to the Board of Revenue, as in reality usurers, disguised as religious friars.

what: Sanyasis got ryots and zamindars into their hands by loans at ruinous interest, then plundered houses and sold children when clients defaulted.
quote: the sanyasis like the Kashmir merchants of to-day got the poor ryots into their hands by loans of money at ruinous rates of interest

what: Sanyasis under Shaw Madginoo fortified places in the Madhupur jungle and at Jamalpur (then Sanyasiganj) in 1781; leaders named include Bibhootgueer, Cherag Aly (a fakir), Donaglin; Jamalpur became the first subdivision in 1845.
quote: The sanyasis under Shaw Madginoo fortified places in the Madhupur Jungle and at Jamalpur (then called Sanyasiganj ) in 1781

what: About 1787 Madhupur was headquarters of a Sanyasi gang under Rup Gir Sanyasi; Sanyasis also had buildings in Boali.
quote: About 1787 it was the head quarters of one of the Sanyasi gangs under Rup Gir Sanyasi.

what: Terrorised zamindars granted rent-free lands for Siva temples; descendants of the Sanyasis still hold them.
quote: The zamindars of the time were terrorised into granting many rent-free lands for the maintenance of temples of Siva and the descendants of the Sanyasis are still in possession.

what: A sanyasi named Jitari is credited with rescuing the pargana from Kamrup (legend).
quote: A sanyasi named Jitari is credited with having rescued this pargana from Kamrup

what: The Mahant of the Raghab Das math at Puri owns part of the pargana, with a cutcherry at Mirga; estate left to the Puri Mahant by will of a Nawab's agent. Raghab Das math is Vaishnava (order not stated in the text).
quote: The Mahant ot the Raghab Das math at Puri owns a part of the pargana with a outcherry at Mirga under a separate Tauzi No. 56.

what: Bairagi Akhra in the forest, scene of an important religious mela; pilgrims from all Mymensingh.
quote: There is a Bairagi Akhra in a secluded spot of the forest, which is almost Himalayan in character, and pilgrims come from all parts of Mymensingh and beyond

what: Important mela that owes its importance to religion more than trade.
quote: An important mela which owes its importance more to religion than to trade takes place at Gupta Brindaban in the Madhupur jungle.

what: Akhra or Vaishnavite monastery at Adampur.
quote: Adampur. — There is an dkhra^ or Vaishnavite monastery

what: Jogi (weaver caste) among Bengali small traders; caste, not ascetic.
